Trivanni Yadav
Ph.D. in Physics, The University of Tulsa (May 2026). I study lithium-ion transport and defect chemistry in solid-state battery materials using density functional theory, and I've spent over a decade teaching undergraduate physics alongside that research. 01 — Research

Defects, diffusion, and the search for a better solid electrolyte

My doctoral work used first-principles density functional theory to study intrinsic point defects and lithium-ion migration in cubic garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO) — a leading candidate solid-state electrolyte for next-generation, non-flammable batteries. Advised by Dr. Sanwu Wang at the University of Tulsa, my thesis asked which defect complexes actually govern how fast lithium can move through the lattice, and why.

VASP CI-NEB Bader Charge Analysis Finite-Size Corrections (sxdefectalign) Machine-Learned Force Fields HPC / Slurm Python Bash VESTA Origin GNU/Linux LaTeX

The work spans electronic-structure analysis, defect-formation thermodynamics across a range of chemical potentials, finite-size corrections for charged defects, and climbing-image NEB calculations of migration barriers — cross-checked against on-the-fly machine-learned force field molecular dynamics. All large-scale calculations ran on HPC clusters (Slurm, Titan, Schooner).

Graduated May 15th, 2026 — doctoral convocation, The University of Tulsa.
